Case 1: Rose Bengal stain in exposed cornea

Head Question:Describe [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Types of dry eye- evaporative vs aq def [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Tests- tbut- schemer- values for both [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Step wise approach- lifestyle, bak free when? antiinflammatory [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Wht else- BCL, amg, tarso [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Elaboration:

Dry Eye Disease (DED):A multifactorial disease of the ocular surface, characterized by a loss of tear film homeostasis. It leads to various ocular symptoms and may be etiologically driven by tear film instability, hyperosmolarity, ocular surface inflammation/damage, and neurosensory abnormalities [AAO 2024 Cornea Subspecialty Day.pdf, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Clinical Presentation:Symptoms include burning, foreign body sensation (FBS), itching, redness, and fluctuating vision [merged_2022experiences.txt, Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition]. Signs include punctate epitheliopathy, filaments, mucus strands, small/absent tear meniscus [Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition].Rose Bengalor lissamine green stains devitalized epithelial cells and mucus on the exposed cornea and conjunctiva [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Types:Broadly classified into:

Aqueous-Deficient Dry Eye (ADDE):Reduced tear production (e.g., Sjögren syndrome, non-Sjögren causes like age, systemic medications, lacrimal gland dysfunction) [AAO 2024 Cornea Subspecialty Day.pdf, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Evaporative Dry Eye (EDE):Excessive tear evaporation (e.g., Meibomian Gland Dysfunction (MGD), blepharitis, rosacea, low blink rate, exposure from lid malposition) [merged_2022experiences.txt, AAO 2024 Cornea Subspecialty Day.pdf, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Investigations (TFOS DEWS II recommended order):

Clinical History/Symptom Questionnaires:(e.g., Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), Dry Eye Questionnaire 5 (DEQ-5)) to assess symptom severity [AAO 2024 Cornea Subspecialty Day.pdf, Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition].

Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT):Measured after fluorescein instillation. ATBUT of <10 secondsis indicative of tear film instability [merged_2022experiences.txt, AAO 2024 Cornea Subspecialty Day.pdf, Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition].

Ocular Surface Staining (Fluorescein, Rose Bengal, Lissamine Green):Grades epithelial damage [merged_2022experiences.txt, AAO 2024 Cornea Subspecialty Day.pdf, Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition].

Schirmer I/II Test:Measures tear production. ASchirmer I test (without anesthetic) of <5 mm over 5 minutesis generally considered abnormal [merged_2022experiences.txt, AAO 2024 Cornea Subspecialty Day.pdf, Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition].

Tear Osmolarity:Elevated osmolarity is a hallmark of DED [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Management (Staged Approach - TFOS DEWS II):

Step 1:Patient education, environmental modifications (e.g., humidifiers, avoiding fans), lifestyle changes (e.g., screen breaks), use ofpreservative-free (BAK-free) artificial tears[merged_2022experiences.txt, Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition].

Step 2:Addition ofanti-inflammatory agents(e.g., topical corticosteroids (short-term), cyclosporine, lifitegrast), tear secretagogues, punctal plugs (temporary or permanent to retain tears) [merged_2022experiences.txt, Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition].

Step 3/4 (for severe/refractory cases):Therapeuticbandage contact lenses (BCL),autologous serum drops (AMG), oral immunomodulators (e.g., doxycycline for MGD), lid hygiene for blepharitis/MGD, surgical interventions liketarsorrhaphyfor severe exposure, or scleral shells [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed., Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition].

Case 2: Band shaped keratopathy

Head Question:Causes- old age, silicone oil, inflammation- JRA [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Management [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Corneal debridement [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Which laser- excimer? Femto [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:How to chelate- edta [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Complications [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Pkp, bcl [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Elaboration:

Band Keratopathy:A corneal degeneration characterized by the deposition ofcalcium phosphate saltsin the superficial cornea (Bowman's layer and anterior stroma), typically in the interpalpebral zone [merged_2022experiences.txt, Basic Principles of Ophthalmic Surgery 4th Ed., The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.]. It appears as a gray-white, Swiss-cheese-like opacity.

Causes/Risk Factors:

Chronic Ocular Inflammation:Most common cause, seen in conditions likeJuvenile Rheumatoid Arthritis (JRA)(now Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis - JIA), chronic uveitis, chronic corneal edema, phthisis bulbi [merged_2022experiences.txt, Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Systemic Hypercalcemia:Hyperparathyroidism, renal failure, sarcoidosis [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Intraocular Silicone Oil:Eyes with silicone oil (e.g., after retinal detachment surgery) can develop band keratopathy [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Age:Can be idiopathic and age-related (senile band keratopathy) [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Topical Medications:Certain phosphate-containing eye drops [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Differential Diagnosis:Urates, iron deposits, other corneal degenerations [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Investigations:Clinical examination with a slit lamp. If a pathological specimen is obtained, Von Kossa stain confirms calcium deposits [Basic Principles of Ophthalmic Surgery 4th Ed.].

Management:

Chelation:Superficial corneal debridementcombined with application ofethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)(1.5-3.0% solution) to chelate and remove the calcium deposits [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Laser:Excimer laser phototherapeutic keratectomy (PTK)can be used to ablate the superficial calcium deposits [merged_2022experiences.txt]. Femtosecond laser is not typically used for this purpose.

Treatment of Underlying Cause:If a systemic condition (e.g., hypercalcemia) or chronic inflammation is present, managing that condition is important [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Surgical:In severe, recurrent, or visually significant cases unresponsive to chelation,Penetrating Keratoplasty (PKP)may be required [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Supportive:Bandage contact lens (BCL)for comfort during healing [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Complications:Recurrence of calcium deposits, corneal scarring, vision loss [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Elaboration:

Ocular Surface Squamous Neoplasia (OSSN):An umbrella term encompassing a spectrum of precancerous and cancerous epithelial lesions of the conjunctiva and cornea, ranging from dysplasia to invasive squamous cell carcinoma [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Clinical Presentation:Highly variable; can appear as a fleshy, gelatinous, leukoplakic (white plaque), orpapillomatous growth[merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf]. Often located at the limbus (nasal or temporal) but can spread onto the cornea or conjunctiva. May have prominent feeder vessels [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Causes/Risk Factors:Ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure,Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection,HIV/AIDS(immunocompromised state), chronic irritation, petroleum exposure [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Differential Diagnosis:Pterygium, pseudopterygium, papilloma (benign), chronic conjunctivitis [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf, Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Investigations:

Slit Lamp Examination with Vital Stains:Fluoresceinor Rose Bengal staining can delineate the often indistinct margins of the lesion, as dysplastic epithelium stains more readily than normal epithelium [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Anterior Segment OCT (AS-OCT):Can show characteristicgross thickening of the epitheliumin OSSN, differentiating it from other lesions like pterygium [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Biopsy:Essential for definitive diagnosis.Excisional biopsywith wide margins is often preferred.Pathologyconfirms squamous cell changes (dysplasia or carcinoma) [merged_2022experiences.txt, Basic Principles of Ophthalmic Surgery 4th Ed.].

Management:

Surgical Excision:"No-touch" technique(to avoid seeding tumor cells) with wide excisional margins. Intraoperative adjuncts includedouble freeze-thaw cryotherapyto the margins and placement of aconjunctival autograftoramniotic membraneto cover the bare sclera [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf, Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P]. Drawing the lesion on filter paper can help map the extent [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Topical Chemotherapy/Immunotherapy:Mitomycin C (MMC), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), or Interferon-alpha2b (IFN-α2b)can be used as primary treatment for small lesions, or as adjuvant therapy after excision to reduce recurrence [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Candidate's Oversight:Could have mentioned serum drops and tarso, sclera/ syblephra ring. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Elaboration:

Chemical Injury:Ocular trauma caused by contact with chemical substances.Alkali burns(e.g., from lye, cement, ammonia, sodium hydroxide (hydroxide)) are generally more severe than acid burns because they rapidly penetrate ocular tissues and cause ongoing damage through saponification [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Emergency Treatment:

Immediate and Copious Irrigation:This is the most critical first step. Irrigate the eye continuously with saline, Ringer's lactate, or even tap water for at least 30 minutes to an hour [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Fornix Sweep:Use a cotton-tipped applicator to sweep the conjunctival fornices to remove any retained particulate matter [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

pH Measurement:Check conjunctival pH usinglitmus paper. Continue irrigation until the pH normalizes to 7.0-7.5 and remains stable for several minutes [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.]. A pH greater than 7 (alkaline) indicates ongoing damage [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Roper Hall Classification:A grading system used to assess the severity of chemical burns based on corneal clarity and the extent oflimbal ischemia. It helps predict visual prognosis and guide further management [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Slit Lamp Examination:Critical for assessing corneal opacity, conjunctival chemosis, and especially the extent oflimbal ischemia(blanching of limbal vessels), which is a key prognostic indicator [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Long-Term Complications:Corneal scarring, corneal vascularization, persistent epithelial defects,dry eye,symblepharon(adhesions between conjunctiva and globe), glaucoma, cataract, and ultimatelyperforation[merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Treatment (Post-Emergency):

Topical Medications:Corticosteroids(to reduce inflammation, but with caution due to risk of corneal melt),antibiotics(to prevent secondary infection),cycloplegics(to reduce pain and synechiae), andvitamin C (ascorbate)(thought to aid collagen synthesis) [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Amniotic Membrane Grafts (AMG):To promote epithelial healing and reduce inflammation and scarring [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Autologous Serum Drops:To provide growth factors and promote healing [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Lid Procedures:Tarsorrhaphy(temporary or permanent partial eyelid closure) for severe exposure, andscleral shells/symblepharon ringsto prevent adhesions [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Limbal Stem Cell Transplantation:For severe limbal stem cell deficiency [AAO 2024 Cornea Subspecialty Day.pdf].

Elaboration:

Conjunctival/Eyelid Papilloma:Benign epithelial tumors of the conjunctiva or eyelids [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Clinical Presentation:Often appear as araspberry-like or sessile lesion, sometimes with a stalk (pedunculated). They can occur on the eyelid margin or conjunctiva, including the nasal quadrant [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf]. Vascularity may be present [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Causes/Risk Factors:Associated withHuman Papillomavirus (HPV) infectionand UV exposure [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Differential Diagnosis (Malignant vs. Benign):It is crucial to differentiate papillomas from malignant lesions such asBasal Cell Carcinoma (BCC)orOcular Surface Squamous Neoplasia (OSSN)[merged_2022experiences.txt].

Features Suggesting Malignancy (BCC/SCC):Irregular margins, ulceration, loss of lashes (madarosis), pearly rolled edges (classic for BCC), deeper infiltration, surrounding tissue damage, involvement of meibomian gland orifices, rapid growth [merged_2022experiences.txt, Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Investigations:

Biopsy:Excisional biopsyis performed for definitive diagnosis and to rule out malignancy. Pathological examination confirms the benign nature or identifies malignancy [merged_2022experiences.txt, Basic Principles of Ophthalmic Surgery 4th Ed.].

Management:

Surgical Excision:Excisionis the primary treatment for papillomas. For eyelid lesions,direct reconstructionof the defect is often performed after excision [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Adjuvant Therapy:For conjunctival papillomas, topical interferon-α2b or cryotherapy may be used to reduce recurrence risk [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Elaboration:

Ectropion:An outward turning of the eyelid margin, most commonly affecting the lower eyelid [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Clinical Presentation (Signs & Symptoms):Exposed palpebral conjunctiva (often red and thickened),foreign body sensation (FBS), chronicepiphora(watering of the eye due to malposition of the punctum and disruption of the tear pump mechanism), and potential forexposure keratopathy(dryness, irritation, and eveninferior corneal ulceration) [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed., The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Types and Causes:

Involutional (Senile) Ectropion:The most common type, caused byage-related horizontal laxityof the eyelid (weakening of the medial and lateral canthal tendons and orbicularis oculi muscle tone) [merged_2022experiences.txt, 07-Oculofacial Plastic and Orbital Surgery.pdf, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Cicatricial Ectropion:Results from scarring and contraction of the skin or underlying tissues of the eyelid (e.g., from trauma, burns, chronic inflammation, skin cancers, previous surgery) [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed., The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Paralytic Ectropion:Caused byfacial nerve (CN VII) palsy, leading to paralysis of the orbicularis oculi muscle and subsequent loss of lid tone and outward sagging [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Mechanical Ectropion:Occurs when a tumor or mass on the eyelid mechanically pulls it away from the globe [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Investigations:Clinical examination, including gross inspection, assessment of lid laxity (e.g., snap-back test), and evaluation of orbicularis oculi function [07-Oculofacial Plastic and Orbital Surgery.pdf, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Management:

Conservative:Lubricating eye drops and ointments, temporary taping of the lid, orbandage contact lens (BCL)for corneal protection [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Surgical:

Involutional Ectropion:Lateral Tarsal Strip (LTS)procedure (tightens the lower eyelid horizontally) often combined with lid shortening procedures [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed., Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Cicatricial Ectropion:Release of scar tissue, often requiring a skin graft (full-thickness or split-thickness) [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Paralytic Ectropion (Facial Nerve Palsy):Initiallyobservationfor spontaneous recovery (e.g., Bell's palsy). If persistent, surgical interventions to correct laxity (e.g., lid-tightening procedures, canthoplasty). Theepiphora may not resolvecompletely if the orbicularis pump mechanism is permanently dysfunctional [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Day 2 Clinical Exam: Neuro and Motility

Case 1: Right eye esotropia. 5-8 year old girl.

Instruction:Candidate performed Hirschberg test, versions, convergences, saccades, pursuits, cover-uncover tests, and found right esotropia with mild restriction in the right eye. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Head Question:Examiner asked candidate to summarize findings and demonstrate restriction. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Asked differentials- ? DRS, right 6 the nerve palsy, congenital/ infantile esotropia. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Elaboration:

Esotropia:(See OSCE Station 2, Case 4 for full elaboration).

Differential Diagnosis for Esotropia with Restriction in a Child:

Duane Retraction Syndrome (DRS):A congenital eye movement disorder characterized byabduction deficit(most common, Type I), globe retraction, and narrowing of the palpebral fissure on attempted adduction. It can mimic a 6th nerve palsy [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Right 6th Cranial Nerve (CN VI) Palsy:Weakness or paralysis of the right lateral rectus muscle, leading to anabduction deficit(inability to move the eye outward) and esotropia that is worse on gaze to the right [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Congenital/Infantile Esotropia:(See OSCE Station 2, Case 4 for full elaboration). This is a primary esotropia usually without restriction.

Accommodative Esotropia:(See OSCE Station 2, Case 4 for full elaboration). Also typically without restriction.

Other considerations for restriction:Orbital masses, restrictive myopathies, prior trauma.

Case 2: Examine face and eyelid.

Instruction:Candidate observed decreased blink rate on left, flat and expressionless left face, rounded angle of mouth on left. Performed VPH, MRD1, eye closure, forehead wrinkles, whistle, smile tests. Diagnosed left facial palsy (Lower Motor Neuron) in a young patient. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Head Question:Asked why you did vph and mrd. Cause of retratction- answered due to decreased orbicularis tone. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Causes- bells, ramsay hunt. Asked to look for cause. Candidate checked neck- found a large vertical scar. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Elaboration:

Facial Nerve (CN VII) Palsy:(See OSCE Station 2, Case 2 for full elaboration).

Lower Motor Neuron (LMN) Palsy:Affects all facial muscles on one side, including the forehead. This causes inability to raise the eyebrow, close the eye, or smile on the affected side [merged_2022experiences.txt, Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Eyelid Retraction with Decreased Orbicularis Tone:The candidate correctly identified that decreased orbicularis oculi tone from facial nerve palsy can lead tomild eyelid retraction(widening of the palpebral fissure) and lagophthalmos, which necessitates checking VPH (vertical palpebral fissure height) and MRD1 (margin reflex distance 1) to assess the degree of exposure and for baseline [merged_2022experiences.txt, 07-Oculofacial Plastic and Orbital Surgery.pdf, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Causes:

Bell's Palsy:Idiopathic LMN facial palsy [merged_2022experiences.txt, Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Ramsay Hunt Syndrome:Herpes zoster virus reactivation in the geniculate ganglion, causing facial palsy with a painful vesicular rash in the ear [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Trauma/Surgery:Alarge vertical neck scarcould indicate prior surgery (e.g., parotidectomy, neck dissection) that potentially injured the facial nerve, leading to iatrogenic palsy [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Other:Tumors (e.g., cerebellopontine angle tumors), infections (e.g., Lyme disease).

Instruction:Candidate performed face position observation, checked for scars/drooping/eyebrow elevation, Hirschberg, MRD, VPH, lagophthalmos. Noted no lid crease, checked LPS action, corneal sensation (absent), Bells phenomenon. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Head Question:How will you counsel this patient- surgery with risk of exposure [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Management plan- discussed frontalis sling- silicone vs facia lata [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:Complications of sling surgery- mentioned all [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:How would you prevent exposure, mentioned frost suture, lubricants and eye gels at night and can tape at night [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Elaboration:

Congenital Ptosis:(See OSCE Station 2, Case 3 for full elaboration).

Examination:Candidate performed a thorough ptosis examination, including observation for compensatory mechanisms, key measurements (MRD, VPH, levator function), and assessment of Bell's phenomenon and corneal sensation, which are crucial for surgical planning and risk assessment [merged_2022experiences.txt, 07-Oculofacial Plastic and Orbital Surgery.pdf, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Counseling:Essential to discuss the surgical plan, potential for improvement, and risks, especiallyexposure keratopathydue to lagophthalmos post-surgery [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Management (Frontalis Sling):

Indication:For poor levator function (<4-5 mm), which is common in significant congenital ptosis [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Materials:Siliconerods (advantages: easy to insert, adjustable, no need for a second surgical site) orautogenous fascia lata(harvested from the thigh, typically for older children) [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Complications of Sling Surgery:Exposure keratopathy/lagophthalmos, infection, granuloma formation, recurrence, asymmetry, under/over-correction [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Prevention of Exposure:Frost suture(a temporary tarsorrhaphy for immediate postoperative protection), frequent lubricants (drops andeye gels at night), and taping the eyelids closed at night [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Marcus Gunn Jaw-Winking Syndrome Management:(See OSCE Station 2, Case 3 for full elaboration). If mild, direct ptosis repair; if severe, levator disinsertion followed by a frontalis sling [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Day 2 Clinical Exam: Anterior Segment

Case 1: Slit lamp examination Old lady – examine the anterior segment of the left eye

Instruction:Candidate adjusted slit lamp, performed diffuse exam, assessed lids, conjunctiva, AC depth (by von Herick's), and identified a tube in the anterior chamber superiorly, an IOL in place with a non-reacting pupil, posterior synechiae, IOL pitting, and prior YAG capsulotomy. Commented on the tube and drainage implant in the superior temporal quadrant. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Head Question:What are the potential complications? Mentioned immediate post op ac shallowing, tube corneal touch and endothelial damage, tube migration, exposure and scleral necrosis, tube blockage by iris or vitreous. [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Sub-Header Question:What will you do to prevent the exposure? And is the implant exposed in this? [merged_2022experiences.txt]

Elaboration:

Glaucoma Drainage Device (Tube Implant):Surgical device (e.g., Baerveldt, Ahmed valve) implanted to lower intraocular pressure (IOP) by diverting aqueous humor from the anterior chamber to a subconjunctival plate [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Clinical Findings:A tube visible in the anterior chamber, often leading to a drainage plate in the superior temporal quadrant. Associated findings like posterior synechiae (adhesions between iris and lens), IOL pitting, and prior YAG capsulotomy suggest a history of complicated intraocular inflammation or surgery [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Potential Complications (Tube-Related):

Early Postoperative:Shallow anterior chamber (AC), hypotony, choroidal detachment, hyphema, tube obstruction.

Late Postoperative:

Corneal Endothelial Damage:Fromtube-corneal touch(the tube rubbing against the corneal endothelium), which can lead to corneal edema and decompensation [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Tube Migration:The tube can shift from its intended position.

Exposure:Exposure of the tube or platethrough the conjunctiva, posing a significant risk for infection (endophthalmitis/blebitis) and scleral necrosis [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Tube Blockage:By iris, vitreous, fibrin, or scar tissue [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Infection:Endophthalmitis, blebitis.

Prevention of Exposure:Meticulous surgical technique, including covering the tube with a scleral patch graft (e.g., donor sclera, pericardium) and ensuring secure, tension-free conjunctival closure over the implant [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Elaboration:

Corneal Scar / Keratoconus / Acute Corneal Hydrops:

Corneal Scar:A permanent opacification of the cornea resulting from prior injury, infection (e.g., corneal ulcer), or disease. A"leucomatous" scaris dense and white, completely obscuring vision [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Keratoconus:A progressive, non-inflammatory corneal ectatic disease where the cornea thins and protrudes into a conical shape, causing irregular astigmatism and vision loss [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Acute Corneal Hydrops:A sudden, vision-threatening complication of advanced keratoconus, occurring when Descemet's membrane ruptures, allowing aqueous humor to acutely enter and opacify the corneal stroma [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.]. This eventually resolves, leaving a dense corneal scar.

Clinical Presentation (Keratoconus):Progressive vision reduction, irregular astigmatism. Signs includeMunson's sign(indentation of the lower eyelid by the conical cornea on downgaze), Fleischer ring (iron deposition at the base of the cone), prominent corneal nerves, and Vogt's striae (vertical stromal folds) [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Differential Diagnosis of Corneal Scarring:Post-corneal ulcer, trauma, corneal dystrophy (e.g., Fuchs' endothelial dystrophy, lattice dystrophy) [merged_2022experiences.txt, 08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Investigations:

Slit Lamp Examination:For direct visualization of the scar, Munson's sign, prominent nerves, stromal folds. History of corneal hydrops would explain a dense scar with keratoconus [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Examine the Other Eye:Keratoconus is typically bilateral, though often asymmetrical. Look for signs of keratoconus or previous corneal surgery (e.g., transplant) in the fellow eye [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Corneal Topography/Tomography:Essential for diagnosing and monitoring keratoconus, showing characteristic steepening and thinning [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

OCT Corneal Epithelial Mapping:Can detect subtle changes in early keratoconus [08-External Disease and Cornea.pdf].

Management:

Early/Non-Progressive:Refractive correctionwith glasses orrigid gas permeable (RGP) contact lenses[merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Progressive Keratoconus:Corneal Cross-Linking (CXL or C3R)is advised to halt disease progression by strengthening corneal collagen [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Advanced Disease/Severe Scarring/Uncorrectable Vision:

Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty (DALK):Replaces the anterior corneal stroma, preserving the patient's own Descemet's membrane and endothelium. This is preferred if the endothelium is healthy (e.g., after healed hydrops) [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Penetrating Keratoplasty (PKP):A full-thickness corneal transplant, used if Descemet's membrane is compromised or with severe scarring [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Elaboration:

Choroidal Coloboma (Coloboma of the Optic Disc/Choroid):A congenital anomaly resulting from incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure during development. It manifests as a defect in the optic disc, retina, or choroid [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed., Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Clinical Presentation:A characteristicwhitish, excavated lesion, typically locatedinferior to the optic discand sometimes involving the disc itself (optic disc coloboma) [merged_2022experiences.txt]. Retinal vessels may appear to "dip into" or disappear within the colobomatous defect [merged_2022experiences.txt]. The optic disc itself can be vertically oval or tilted [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Classification:Not extensively detailed in the provided sources, but it's a developmental defect.

Associated Conditions/Complications:

Refractive Error:Commonly associated withmyopiaand astigmatism [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Visual Acuity:Depends on the involvement of the macula. If the macula is spared, good visual acuity is possible [merged_2022experiences.txt]. However, associatedstrabismus(eye misalignment) andamblyopia(reduced vision due to abnormal visual experience during development, either refractive or strabismic) can cause significant vision loss [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Other Ocular Anomalies:Can be part of syndromes (e.g., CHARGE syndrome) and associated with iris coloboma, microphthalmos, aniridia, or anterior segment dysgenesis [Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P, The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed., The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Retinal Detachment:Serous retinal detachment can occur at the margins of the coloboma [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Investigations:

Dilated Fundus Examination (using 90D lens or indirect ophthalmoscopy):To visualize and characterize the coloboma [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Refraction:To identify and correct any refractive errors [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Anterior Segment Examination:To look for other associated ocular anomalies [merged_2022experiences.txt].

B-scan Ultrasonography:If media opacities preclude direct visualization or to evaluate for retinal detachment [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Management:

Refractive Correction:Prescribe glasses for any myopia or astigmatism [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Amblyopia Therapy:Essential if present, involving patching or atropine penalization [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Monitoring:Regular follow-up to monitor for complications like retinal detachment [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Elaboration:

Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP):A group of inherited progressive retinal dystrophies characterized by primary degeneration of photoreceptors (initially rods, then cones) and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Clinical Presentation:

Symptoms:Earliest symptom is oftennight blindness (nyctalopia), followed by progressiveperipheral visual field loss(leading to "tunnel vision"), and eventually central vision loss [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed., Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Signs (Fundus):Classic triad includeswaxy pallor of the optic disc,attenuation of retinal vessels(especially arterioles), and characteristicbone-spicule-shaped retinal pigmentation(pigmented cells aggregating in the mid-periphery and later extending to the macula) [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed., Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P]. Macular involvement with pigmentation and pallor is a late sign [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Causes/Risk Factors:Predominantlygenetic, with various inheritance patterns (autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked, mitochondrial) [merged_2022experiences.txt, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Complications:Cystoid Macular Edema (CME), posterior subcapsular cataract, epiretinal membrane, vitreous cells/syneresis [merged_2022experiences.txt, 09-Uveitis and Ocular Inflammation.pdf, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed.].

Investigations:

Visual Acuity and Refraction:To assess current vision and correct refractive errors [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Visual Fields:To map and monitor progressive peripheral and central vision loss [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Electroretinogram (ERG):A definitive diagnostic test, showingreduced or extinguished a- and b-waves, reflecting photoreceptor dysfunction [merged_2022experiences.txt, Oxford Handbook of Ophthalmology 4th edition, The Ophthalmology Examinations Review Tien Yin WONG 3rd Ed., Past cadidate Exp-All chua + missing in chua - 429P].

Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT):To detect and monitorCMEand evaluate the structural integrity of the outer retina and RPE [merged_2022experiences.txt, 09-Uveitis and Ocular Inflammation.pdf].

Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF):To visualize areas of RPE atrophy and lipofuscin accumulation [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Genetic Testing:Can identify the specific gene mutation, aiding in diagnosis and genetic counseling [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Management:

Supportive Care:

Refractive correction:Glasses for any refractive errors [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Cataract Surgery:If a visually significant cataract (common complication) is present [merged_2022experiences.txt].

CME Treatment:Oral acetazolamide (Diamox)or topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitors can reduce CME and improve vision in some cases [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Low Vision Aids:For significant vision impairment [The Wills Eye Manual 8th Ed.].

Genetic Counseling:To inform patients about inheritance patterns, prognosis, and potential for future therapies [merged_2022experiences.txt].

Experimental Treatments:Gene therapies and retinal prostheses are actively being investigated [12-Retina and Vitreous.pdf].
